title: Navigating the Climate Labyrinth: A Dual Approach to Insurance Resilience and Landmark Defense

context_sources.name: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

limitations: A MATHmodels watermark of repeated glyphs runs through every page and through the equations.
Equations 1 to 15 print with exponents and subscripts detached from their bases.
The contents page scrambles the section numbers, and the running header says 25 pages while the document has 28.
Table 3 places the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics in a different order from the p-values.
Table 5 assigns second-level indicators to the wrong first-level headings.
The summary counts two first-level and eight second-level indicators; the body uses three and ten.

tasks: Decide whether an insurer should underwrite in a region of rising extreme weather
Adapt that model so a developer can choose where and how to build
Score landmarks by value and risk and assign each a preservation strategy
Write the community a one-page letter with the schedule, the plan, and the cost

section_map.summary: Two ruin ranges, a three-city ranking, and a five-level preservation scale.
A quotation from Bill Gates and a protection gap of 57 percent.
Four tasks, the last a one-page letter.
Coverage of 45 percent against 7 percent, then a one-line synthesis.
Three assumptions, each with a justification line.
Mumbai and Cairns chosen, each with its own weather.
A Pareto tail, a logistic frequency, and a ruin probability.
Four risk bands, Mumbai rising faster than Cairns.
Houston ahead of New Orleans ahead of Miami.
Value against risk on a GE matrix, five levels of strategy.
Level A, with flooding priced at 237 million dollars a year.
A 10 percent capital shock moves ruin by about 2 percent.
Three measures and a cost in the millions.
Six logged uses, one of them without a query.

contributions.summary: Only the losses beyond a threshold chosen from the Hill plot are fitted.
A constant disaster frequency is replaced by a logistic curve once it contradicts the trend.
The ruin formula is turned into an optimal retention and an optimal investment.
The ruin probability becomes one indicator inside a development score.
Nine sectors of a GE matrix collapse into five preservation levels, each with a strategy.

dependency_graph.handoff: The probability of ruin enters the insurance dimension of the development score.
The probability of ruin is reused as the risk that a landmark is uninsured.

assumptions.summary: Catastrophe insurance is independent of other lines of business.
The insurer can reinsure and can invest the funds.
Every policy carries a deductible borne by the holder.
Disaster frequency would be Poisson if it were not rising.
Human intervention will eventually cap the frequency of disasters.
A landmark's value and risk behave like market attractiveness and competitiveness.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Compensations in Mumbai and Cairns from 2000 to 2022, rescaled to 2022 prices by the CPI.
The sample is expanded to 1023 points by Monte Carlo simulation.
A threshold of 2.26 leaves 69 exceedances, 6.74 percent of the sample.
Indicator data for Miami, New Orleans, and Houston, projected a decade ahead.
Thirty-five coastal landmarks scored on value and risk.
OECD projections for Boston flooding, 237 million dollars a year to 2050.

models.summary: Prices a region by the probability that the insurer is ruined.
Ranks cities by a development index that includes the ruin probability.
Places landmarks on a value-risk matrix and assigns a strategy.

verification.summary: Three candidate distributions are compared by p-value and the largest wins.
Four count distributions are tested and only the Poisson passes at 5 percent.
A 10 percent change in capital moves the ruin probability by about 2 percent.
Noise added to the preservation indicators does not change the urgency level.

results_trace.summary: The tail is fit with scale 2.929 and shape -0.499.
Mumbai's ruin probability rises from 3.71 to 12.22 percent and Cairns's from 1.33 to 4.40.
Houston ranks first for development potential, then New Orleans, then Miami.
Faneuil Hall falls in level A, the most urgent.
Boston flooding is priced at 237 million dollars a year, covering 6 percent of the city.

writing_logic.summary: Name the three jobs as verbs before naming any model.
Report a forecast as a move from one level to the next, with the range.
Give every assumption a justification line of its own.
Number the procedure as steps so it can be repeated.
State the contradiction, then replace the assumption.
Rewrite the formula as numbered rules the company can follow.
Concede the weakness of the winning option before recommending it.
Close the letter on the community's action, not on the budget.

language_observations.summary: The threshold is defended by naming both mistakes it avoids, too high and too low.
The new curve is introduced as inspired by population growth, so the analogy is visible.
Each sub-rule names the quantity the insurer must look up.
A tool from business strategy is justified by a one-sentence analogy before it is used.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1 maps extreme weather events across recent decades.
Figure 2 draws the whole argument as one flowchart.
Figures 3 and 4 map the weather of Mumbai and of Cairns.
Figure 5 shows the expanded sample and its fitted curve.
Figure 7 is the exponential Q-Q plot used to judge the tail.
Figure 8 compares the fitted frequency densities and Figure 9 projects them.
Figure 10 plots the predicted ruin probability for both cities.
Figures 11 and 12 draw the indicator system as a network and as a hierarchy.
Figure 13 projects the development index and Figure 14 compares the indicators.
Figure 15 shows the combined weights for value and for risk.

Figure 18 pairs the sensitivity test with the robustness test.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge rewards a paper that drops an assumption once it contradicts the data.
A judge rewards a formula restated as rules a practitioner can follow.
A judge penalizes a weighting whose comparison matrices are omitted.

weaknesses.summary: The summary counts two first-level and eight second-level indicators; the body has three and ten.
The frequency-test table orders its statistics differently from its p-values.
The weight table assigns indicators to the wrong headings, and the matrices are omitted.
Two different precipitation counts are given the same symbol.
The prose assigns value to both axes and risk to the vertical axis in the same breath.
The model is called sensitive and robust in a single paragraph.
The loss sample is multiplied to 1023 by simulation before any fit.

independent_extensions.statement: Refit the generalized Pareto tail to the 69 real exceedances alone and compare with the fit on the simulated 1023.
independent_extensions.reason: The paper expands the sample by Monte Carlo before estimating, so the fit may reproduce the simulation rather than the data.

independent_extensions.statement: Price each of the five preservation strategies and add the cost to the letter.
independent_extensions.reason: The paper itself concedes that the measures are given without their cost.

candidate_rule_impacts.impact: Supports replacing a constant disaster frequency with a logistic curve once the trend contradicts it.
Supports pricing a region by the probability of ruin and feeding that probability into both the siting score and the preservation score.

unresolved_questions: Whether the Pareto shape stays negative when the fit uses only the real exceedances.
Which second-level indicators actually sit under each heading, since the table and the prose disagree.
What the five preservation strategies cost.
